decisions.actualImageObservation: Native pixels show a reactive hydroxide O pair aimed at terminal C of Br-CH2-CH2-Br; a second curved arrow moves the C-Br pair to Br. First-stage product is HO-CH2-CH2-Br +Br-minus. The green lower panel explicitly labels the diol as after a second substitution. No H-origin attack, instantaneous replacement of both Br by one hydroxide or added proton transfer is pictured. Only the reactive pair is depicted, not an asserted complete Lewis shell.
decisions.wholeDutyCompatibility: This is a correct shorter illustrative member of the supplied elementary primary-C substitution model. It supports, without contradicting, attack/departure, retained O-H, the stopped monohydroxy intermediate and eventual two-OH functionality. The unchanged goal and cases still require both local arrow pairs, whole atom/charge balance and explanation of monomer suitability. No image claim of real yield or uniquely established full reaction pathway is adopted.
decisions.case1: The picture uses the two-carbon example, whereas the full case requires the six-carbon substrate and bromoethane comparison. Copying the picture cannot establish both complete six-carbon steps and minus2 balance or explain why ethanol caps a chain rather than providing the same diol bridge. e4 is still an actual changed-functionality inference.
decisions.case2: The full three-carbon stopped X, both faulty draft diagnoses and the one-equivalent molecular-distribution assertion remain distinct demands. The picture teaches the local pattern already stipulated in material but supplies neither the dosage-distribution inference nor the requested complete three-carbon account. Chain renaming alone is still not counted as independent transfer.
decisions.assessmentBoundary: An explanatory learning-goal image can scaffold the local model. It does not replace learner construction/explanation or satisfy the rubric automatically. No additional task quota, new prerequisite or physical synthesis duty is introduced.

decisions.wholeDutyCompatibility: The illustration supports the introductory distinction between acid component and aqueous solution plus conditional use and handling from actual information. Conservative no-mixing pictogram is read with the supplied rule against unknown cleaners, not as a contradiction of dissolving the identified acid in its stated water solvent.
